content.comment_body: Hello. I want to transfer the state of a flag over the network from one [product_name] module to another. In my example, I am reading the M39 flag. Could someone explain how to easily determine which memory byte (MB) and bit should be accessed for other flags, such as M53?
MB0 = M1 - M8 MB1 = M9 - M16 MB2 = M17 - M24 MB3 = M25 - M32 MB4 = M33 - M40 MB5 = M41 - M48 MB6 = M49 - M56 MB7 = M57 - M64 See attachment.
Thank you! The explanation in the Help documentation confused me.

Is this related to a [article_no]? Yes, the number of memory bytes depends on the available flags. For instance, [article_no] has 27 flags, so only MB0-MB3 are used. [article_no] includes 64 flags, covering MB0-MB7.
The manual mentions: "[article_no] and later versions only".

At the time of writing, [article_no] was most likely the current [product_name] module. Perhaps [company_name] hadn't anticipated that [article_no] would eventually support 64 flags instead of only 27. I am not concerned about this detail.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing how to identify the correct memory byte and bit when transferring flag states between [product_name] modules over a network. The main user experience challenge is vagueness in documentation, especially regarding how flags map to memory bytes across different hardware versions. Users express confusion due to changes in product features and insufficiently clear guidance.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward and easily accessible information or tools that allow them to quickly determine the appropriate memory byte and bit for specific flag numbers across all versions of [product_name].
